full_judgment:
7. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that having regard to the facts that the property in question was owned by Solaiman Pasha who being the real owner having transferred the same by executing registered sale deeds to the petitioner and others on receipt of valuable consideration, the inclusion of the property in the 'Kha' list of abandoned buildings under section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 by the Government was illegal and in that view of the matter the order of the respondent No. 2 is without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect. It is argued that the purchase documents being valid documents the presumption of validity and authenticity of transfer is attached with the same, and therefore, the order of the respondent No. 2 dismissing the appeal without taking into consideration this aspect of the matter and the law involved therein is to be held to have been passed without jurisdiction and of no legal effect. Mr. Khan Saidur Rahman submits that the possession of the property by Sangstha, an unauthorised occupant, does not render the premises to be treated as abandoned property. It is also submitted that at the time while the transfer was made by registered document Solaiman Pasha was the owner of the property and the petitioner having acquired title by way of purchase from the person having valid title mere inclusion of the property in the 'Kha' list of the property does not render the sale invalid so as to bring the property within the mischief of abandoned property. The learned advocate submits that the inclusion of the property in the 'Kha' list of abandoned property without serving any notice to the petitioner in contravention of the provision of section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 is illegal and without jurisdiction. The learned Advocate also submits that mere non occupation of the property by the owner at the time of transfer will not render it as abandoned property. The learned Advocate further contends that a person being the owner of the property may remain temporarily away from the property living somewhere in the country but such temporary absence of the owner will not divest him of the title in the property and the right to transfer. The learned Advocate has cited the case of Sultanuddin Chowdhury Vs. Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others reported in 32 DLR 252 wherein it is held: 

 "A kabala executed and registered in Bangladesh in 1975 creates a presumption that the registration authority was satisfied that the executants was a valid citizen and national of Bangladesh since an Indian National as such could not transfer any property in Bangladesh by way of any registered deed." 

 8. It is true that a registered kabala carries with it a prima facie presumption of title of the parties to the kabala but this presumption is rebuttable by evidence. In the instant case it has been found by the learned Court of Settlement from the evidence on record that the real owner was not in possession of the premises in the year 1983. There is nothing on record to show that Solaiman Pasha ever moved the appropriate authority for restoration of possession of the premises in his favour and from this the learned court has drawn inference that the whereabouts of Solaiman Pasha was unknown in November, 1985 while the sale deeds were alleged to have been executed. It was further found by the learned Court of Settlement that none of the witnesses have had any acquaintance with Solaiman Pasha prior to the execution and registration of the Kabalas. In such circumstances, doubt arises regarding the identity of Solaiman and for that matter it was further held that since the real owner did not file any application till 1985 it would be deemed that he was not within Bangladesh after the liberation. 

 16. So by operation of section 5(2) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 the inclusion of the property in question in the 'Kha' list as abandoned property and publication of the same in the official Gazette is conclusive evidence of the fact that the property is abandoned and has vested in the Government. The presumption arising out of sub-section 2 of section 5 of the Ordinance No LIV of 1985 that the Gazette is conclusive evidence of the fact that the building in question in abandoned and has vested in the Government has not been rebutted by the petitioner.
